_provenance.note: LLM reading of the lens token tables; not a measurement

axes.label: 20th-century (1910s–1960s) ↔ Baroque/Enlightenment era (1600s–1700s)
axes.rationale: All three lenses put year prefixes 161–175 and ' Enlightenment' on the positive end, and 189–196 plus ' Soviet', ' WWII', ' Nazi' and '昭和' (Shōwa era) on the negative end; the real-logit correlation shows only uninformative function words.

axes.label: WWII-era mid-20th century ↔ Romantic/Napoleonic 19th century (1780s–1880s)
axes.rationale: All three lenses agree: the positive end is 179–187 with ' Victorian' and ' Napoleon', and the negative end is ' WWII', ' Hitler', ' Stalin', ' Eisenhower' and 192–195, isolating 19th-century births from the 1930s–40s; the real-logit correlation shows only function words.

axes.label: 18th-century Classical era (1660s–1770s) ↔ late 19th century / medieval
axes.rationale: All three lenses put 166–177 and ' Enlightenment' on the negative end; the positive end mixes late-1800s prefixes (185–189, ' Victorian') with medieval tokens (' Dante', ' medieval', ' Byz', '146'/'125'), so this axis appears to contrast 18th-century births with dates further from that era in either direction.
